title: Mid-Day ETF Update: ETFs, Stocks Weaker, Weighed by Lackluster Data From US, China; Johnson & Johnson Leads Health Care Lower

organizations.name: johnson & johnson leads health care lower shutterstock

text:
Shutterstock photo Active broad-market exchange-traded funds in Friday's regular session:
iShares MSCI Emerging Index Fund ( EEM ): -0.8%
SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ): -1.3%
SPDR Select Sector Fund - Financial ( XLF ): -0.5%
iShares MSCI EAFE ETF ( EFA ): -1%
Invesco QQQ Trust, Series 1 ( QQQ ): -1.5%
Broad Market Indicators
Broad-market exchange-traded funds, including IWM and IVV were weaker. Actively traded PowerShares QQQ ( QQQ ) was down 1.5%.
US stocks continued to trade in the negative territory at session's half, after downbeat Chinese economic data drove worries about global growth while the figures from the world's biggest economy offered a mixed, but slightly more upbeat, picture.
China reportedly released November retail sales and industrial output data that missed expectations. Back home, the US slate of data was mixed, with retail sales for November rising 0.2% month-to-month, beating expectations for 0.1% growth to indicate a strong start to the holiday shopping season. October's business inventories rose 0.6%, in line with expectations, while business sales were up 0.3%.
November industrial production in the US also topped expectations, coming in at 0.6% against views for 0.3%. But the December flash manufacturing PMI declined to a 13-month low of 53.9 and the services reading dropped to an 11-month low of 53.4.
The health care sector retreated, weighed by Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) -- shares of the company plunged after Reuters reported that it knew for decades about asbestos in its baby powder products.
Power Play: Health Care
Health Care SPDR (XLV) was down 3% while other health care funds including Vanguard Health Care ETF (VHT) and iShares Dow Jones U.S. Healthcare (IYH) were lower. Biotechnology fund iShares NASDAQ Biotechnology Index (IBB) was down 1.2%.
Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) didn't disclose to regulators or the public that the company's talc and finished powders tested positive for small amounts of asbestos from at least 1971 to the early 2000s, Reuters reported, citing a review of documents and testimony. The information was contained in thousands of pages of company documents and other confidential papers released to lawyers for some of the thousands of plaintiffs alleging that the talc has caused their cancers, the news service said. JNJ shares fell more than 8%.
Winners and Losers
Financial
The Select Financial Sector SPDRs ( XLF ) was down 0.5%. Direxion Daily Financial Bull 3X shares (FAS) was down 1.7% and its bearish counterpart Direxion Daily Financial Bear 3X shares (FAZ) was up 2%.
Draper Oakwood Technology Acquisition Inc. (DOTA) sank nearly 41% after it said it has entered into two backstop arrangements in connection with its proposed business combination with Reebonz Ltd. The business combination, if approved by the stockholders of the company, will be effected pursuant to an agreement among Draper Oakwood, Reebonz Ltd. and DOTA Holdings Ltd., and will be renamed Reebonz Holding Ltd. Draper Oakwood and DOTA Holdings Ltd. entered into backstop agreements with two different accredited investors. One investor has agreed to acquire 1 million shares of Class A common stock of the company, and the other investor has agreed to acquire $5 million of shares of common stock in the open market or in privately negotiated transactions.
Technology
Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) was down 1.7%, while tech funds iShares Dow Jones US Technology ETF (IYW) was up and iShares S&P North American Technology ETF (IGM) was in the red.
Among semiconductor ETFs, SPDR S&P Semiconductor (XSD) was down 0.6% and Semiconductor Sector Index Fund (SOXX) was down 0.6%.
Apple (AAPL) fell more than 2% after reports that the company plans to push software updates to some of its devices in China as it seeks to address Qualcomm's (QCOM) accusations of patent infringement that prompted the Fuzhou Intermediate People's Court last week to ban the sale of as many as seven of its iPhones in the world's most populous nation. Apple will carry out the software updates at the start of next week, Reuters reported, citing a company statement.
Energy
Dow Jones US Energy Fund (IYE) was down 2.0% and Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) was down 1.9%.
Camber Energy (CEI) fell nearly 4% after it said it has been granted an extension to comply with the NYSE listing rule that requires a minimum of $6 million in stockholders' equity. The extension is through Feb. 3, subject to compliance with initiatives outlined by the company. The company will be subject to periodic review during the extended plan period, according to a statement.
Commodities
Crude was down 2.8%. United States Oil Fund (USO) was down 3.0%. Natural gas down 4.8% while United States Natural Gas Fund (UNG) was down 6.8%.
Gold was down 0.3%. SPDR Gold Trust (GLD) was down 0.3%. Silver was down 1.2%, while iShares Silver Trust (SLV) was down 1%.
Consumer
Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR (XLP) was down 1.4% and Vanguard Consumer Staples ETF (VDC) and iShares Dow Jones U.S. Consumer Goods (IYK) were lower.
Meanwhile, Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR (XLY) was down 1% while retail funds SPDR S&P Retail (XRT) and Market Vectors Retail ETF (RTH) were weaker.
Sears Holdings (SHLDQ), the beleaguered retailer that filed for bankruptcy two months ago, has seen shoppers flock to the closing-out sales in the locations that are being shuttered as part of the company's reorganization. In the 13-week period ending Nov. 3, comparable-store sales rose 4.3%, the department store operator said in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Friday. Comps for its Kmart unit jumped 6.1% in the third quarter while Sears Domestic was up 3.2%. In the same period of last year, Sears reported total plunge of 15% in comparable sales, while Kmart's comps were down 13% and Sears stores declined 17%. SHLDQ shares were up 8.6%.
